messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated 99th latency + increased error rates on /v1/generate (dedicated pools). Service: kv-cache. Suspected cause: cache spilling / continuous-batching surge. Runbooks attached: /runbooks/kv-cache-paging, /runbooks/disable-batching. Paging: @ashley (oncall-ml) @maria (oncall-sre)

ashley: I'm on it. Dashboards show per-shard resident size increasing quickly on TP layout gpugrp-09. Several ranks are hitting swap/spill-to-host alerts.

maria: I see NCCL timeouts and reconnection loops in runtime logs. Example:
```
[2026-03-15T12:14:02Z] ERROR nccl: op alltoallv failed, retrying
[2026-03-15T12:14:08Z] WARN nccl: barrier wait > 150ms
[2026-03-15T12:14:10Z] ERROR vm: page-fault flood detected on /dev/nvme0n1
```

ashley: correlating with deploy history: a continuous-batching rollout at 09:00 raised concurrent_prefixes from 16->64 and enabled immediate_insert=true. That increases simultaneous KV inserts.

tess: customer impact: two Dedicated customers in eu-west reported degraded throughput and intermittent 5xx. CS requeued requests and opened tickets.

liam: Observed pattern: when concurrent_prefixes > 32, certain shard hashes cluster on tensor rank subset due to an old modulo-based sharder. That causes hot partitioning under heavy batching.

ashley: Hypothesis: batching surge -> heavy simultaneous prefix inserts -> hot shard -> local memory pressure -> paging -> NCCL stalls -> whole TP job stalls -> request errors.

maria: Live mitigation options: A) disable continuous batching globally for affected pools, B) throttle insert rate per-shard, C) restart TP jobs to break NCCL stuck state. I'd prefer A then C.

ashley: agreed. Plan: 1) set continuous_batching=false on pool gpupool-dedicated-eu-1, 2) restart runtimes on gpugrp-09 after verifying no new NCCL timeouts, 3) roll back concurrent_prefixes to 16.

liam: running step 1 now:
```
infractl pool patch gpupool-dedicated-eu-1 --continuous_batching=false --reason "incident mitigation"
```

ops-bot: Action accepted. Patch queued to control plane; request id 0a9f.

liam: control-plane confirms change. Batcher backlog fell from 9k -> 1.8k in 60s.

maria: scheduling runtime restarts. On gpugrp-09 I'm cordoning rank 5 then restarting runtime process to clear NCCL peer state. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpugrp-09-n5
kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpugrp-09-n5
```

maria: restart done. Logs show NCCL reconverged. No new allreduce timeouts in last 45s.

ashley: after mitigations, 99p latency improved from 2.6s -> 380ms, errors dropped from 6% -> 0.5%. Still above baseline.

tess: CS update sent. They asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

liam: short-term safety patch: will submit a throttler that adds jitter to per-rank inserts and enforces per-shard max_inserts_per_sec=1200. Also drop immediate_insert feature when TP is enabled. Creating PR.

ashley: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5009 (adds per-rank insert jitter + TP-aware sharding guard). Requesting expedited review.

maria: config rollback initiated for concurrent_prefixes:
```
configctl set service.batch.concurrent_prefixes=16 --env prod --reason "rollback after paging incident"
```

maria: rollout succeeded. Monitoring: no additional spill events on gpugrp-* pools.

liam: opened follow-up tickets: INF-8201 (add per-shard insertion metrics), INF-8202 (audit sharder for modulo skew), INF-8203 (add canary gating on batching toggles).

ashley: for postmortem: need heap dumps from ranks that spilled, NCCL traces, and the list of pools that had continuous_batching enabled at the time. I'll coordinate the data collection.

maria: handoff: oncall-sre will monitor for 6 hours and validate patch rollout. I'm assigning follow-up ownership to @liam for the code fix and to @tess for customer comms.

tess: ack. Drafted customer note: we've applied mitigations and will deploy patch within 6 hours. Offering a goodwill credit if SLA impacted.

ops-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated. Severity: high. Owner: ashley. Postmortem due: 2026-03-17T20:00:00Z.

ashley: leaving the channel. Thanks for the quick coordination. We'll keep watchers on the alert.
